summary.headline: H1 FY27 consolidated PAT rose 36.8% YoY to INR14.3 crores, the company's highest first half, on revenue up 29.6% to INR34.2 crores.
summary.overview: Pune E-Stock Broking reported H1 FY27 (six months to 30 September 2026) consolidated revenue from operations of INR34.2 crores, up 29.6% YoY and 24% HoH, with PBT of INR19.1 crores (+38.8%) and PAT of INR14.3 crores (+36.8%). Net profit margin was 41.7%, up 220 bps YoY but down from about 50% in H2 FY26. Management said the quarter was shaped by a weak secondary market (F&O volume cuts, higher STT in April 2026) and used the call to position MTF, merchant banking, insurance distribution and AIF as fee-based growth drivers, most of which are only months old and contribute little revenue yet. Equity rose to INR225 crores from INR180.6 crores in March, helped by warrant conversions and a new warrant issue.

segments.name: Broking and MTF
segments.commentary: Foundation business; MTF book crossed INR100 crores, fully collateralised by client shares and cash, and is being grown 'carefully'. Short-term borrowings (INR65 crores) mainly fund the MTF book.

segments.name: Research
segments.commentary: Team of MBAs, CAs, economists and CFAs; curated equity basket lets clients invest in a research team's ideas with a single order. No revenue split disclosed.

segments.name: Mutual fund distribution
segments.commentary: Works with 36 AMCs and more than 500 schemes; over 1,600 investors, AUM above INR240 crores, SIP book over INR1.5 crores. Capital-light, fee-based, recurring.

segments.name: PESB Alpha Fund (Cat III AIF) / PESB Asset Management LLP
segments.commentary: Launched November 2025, about INR55 crores under management; PESB invested INR15 crores. Management claims about 25% post-fee, post-tax return in year one; income accrues to the wholly owned fund-manager LLP. Clients typically commit for at least three years.

segments.name: Merchant banking
segments.commentary: Licence obtained about a year ago (2025); first fees earned in 2026. First mandate Apar Advertisers (SME) approved and expected to list within a couple of months; several other SME and mainboard mandates in pipeline. No fee figures disclosed.

segments.name: Insurance distribution (Pune Finvest / QURA Insure)
segments.commentary: Pune Finvest (79.8% subsidiary) received IRDAI corporate agency approval in July 2026; advisory operations began September 2026 under the QURA Insure brand, initially targeting the existing 65,000 clients. No revenue disclosed.

guidance_outlook: Improve return ratios as fee-based businesses (wealth, merchant banking, insurance, AIF) scale; management expects ROE and ROCE to move up steadily but gave no targets.
Grow to more than 1 lakh customers by 2027 (client base currently above 65,000, of whom above 17,000 are traded clients).

Plans: open flagship branches in high-visibility locations, grow the MTF book carefully, scale an open API-based algo trading platform for retail, and build GIFT City merchant banking, secured lending and insurance businesses.

Warrant proceeds (16 lakh warrants at INR234 each, 25% received) to be deployed mainly in MTF and merchant banking; branches and technology funded as needed; promoters participated in the warrant round so dilution is limited.
capex_capacity: Capital allocation is driven by MTF book growth and merchant banking; branch and technology spend is 'on need basis' per management.
Warrant issue: 16 lakh convertible warrants at INR234 each, 25% of subscription received; 18 lakh equity shares issued on warrant conversion during H1.
Dividend: final dividend of INR1 per share for FY26 paid.
PESB committed INR15 crores to PESB Alpha Fund; AIF size about INR55 crores.
Planned flagship branches in high-visibility locations; no count or timelines disclosed.
demand_pricing: Industry context: SEBI F&O measures more than halved option volumes in 2026 and cut individual F&O traders by about a fifth; higher STT on derivatives from April 2026 added pressure.
Industry margin trading book rose from above INR1.4 lakh crores (June 2026) to about INR1.6 lakh crores (September 2026), per management.
Mainboard IPOs raised a record INR94,200 crores across 78 issues in H1 CY26 (35% higher YoY per management); total IPO fundraise including SME exceeded INR1 lakh crores.
Management expects margins on insurance to fall under IRDAI commission-cap proposals but volumes to rise; sees MTF rule tightening as a long-term positive that reduces speculation in weak scrips.

Management said the call's market backdrop was weak: Nifty about 1% up for H1, down about 6% in September; FIIs net sellers of over INR2.3 lakh crores in April-September 2026; domestic institutions bought about INR3.9 lakh crores.

qa_highlights.question: What is the view on merchant banking and the IPO pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Ronak Jhaveri said the first mandate, Apar Advertisers (SME), is approved and listing is planned within a couple of months; several SME and mainboard mandates are in the pipeline and will be disclosed on BSE as they are signed.

qa_highlights.question: Will share capital increase, where will growth be funded, and how are Pune Finvest, PESB Alpha Fund, PESB Asset Management LLP and IFSC structured?
qa_highlights.answer: Arpit Shah said growth will be funded by internal accruals and the recent warrant issue, mainly into MTF and merchant banking. Pune Finvest is a 79.8% subsidiary holding the NBFC and insurance business; the AIF trust has appointed PESB Asset Management LLP, a wholly owned subsidiary, as fund manager. He did not detail the IFSC entity.

qa_highlights.question: Why a corporate agency licence rather than an insurance broking licence?
qa_highlights.answer: Corporate agency approval came faster from IRDAI, with a consultant's guidance, and the holding-company structure delayed the insurance-company route; management said many NBFCs operate as corporate agents with no major structural difference.

qa_highlights.question: How will warrant proceeds be deployed and how is dilution weighed?
qa_highlights.answer: Proceeds go mainly to MTF and merchant banking, with branches and technology funded as needed. Promoters participated equally in the warrant round, so promoter stake is not expected to dilute materially.

qa_highlights.question: What are the return-ratio drivers and the biggest risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said fee-based businesses are capital-light and returns should improve as they contribute; new licences are only a year old, so contribution is still small. The main risk cited is regulatory change, which is industry-wide, and management said it is confident of coping given over 15 years in the business.

qa_highlights.question: How will IRDAI commission caps and SEBI's MTF rule review affect the business?
qa_highlights.answer: Insurance margins will fall, but volumes should rise; management expects no major issue from MTF rules and said it is prepared if final rules are stricter, with benefits over the long term rather than the short term.

qa_highlights.question: How will cross-selling of mutual fund and advisory products be done, and is it RM-led or digital?
qa_highlights.answer: Management uses RM-led face-to-face coverage for suitability and risk-profiling, backed by a digital team to reach clients in locations without physical presence.

qa_highlights.question: Is AIF fee income lumpy and how will the AIF scale?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AIF fees are consistent because investors commit for at least three years; year one delivered about 25% post-fee, post-tax return, and marketing through RMs and word of mouth is planned.

qa_highlights.question: How is MTF concentration risk managed in a sharp fall, and what is the collateral shortfall record?
qa_highlights.answer: Software tracks positions, MTM and collateral shortfalls, with staff contacting clients; if a shortfall persists for more than five days, the stock is liquidated. No historical shortfall figures were given.

risks_watch: Regulatory risk: SEBI review of MTF rules and IRDAI proposals to cap insurance commissions could compress margins; management called the impact short-term.
Net profit margin fell from about 50% in H2 FY26 to 41.7% in H1 FY27; watch whether this is a trend as new businesses scale.
Weak F&O activity and higher STT on derivatives could keep broking volumes under pressure.
MTF book growth of INR100 crores plus INR65 crores of short-term borrowings raise funding and collateral-shortfall risk in a sharp market fall; no shortfall history was disclosed.
Warrant conversion (16 lakh warrants at INR234) and merchant banking/IPO execution depend on primary-market momentum; the Apar Advertisers listing is a near-term test.
Management gave no quantified revenue targets for new businesses, and merchant banking and insurance revenue was not separately disclosed.
key_quotes: Our consolidated revenue from operations grew around 30% to INR34.2 crores. EBITDA grew by 31% to INR22.3 crores, and net profit grew almost 37% to INR14.3 crores, our highest for any first half of the year.
We will not pursue growth at any cost. We will build with discipline, invest where we see clear opportunity, and remain mindful of the trust our clients and shareholders place in us.
So yes, we may find a short-term hitch in our profitability or margins, but in the longer term, it is actually working in our favour.
Since these licenses have come just a year back, there is no significant contribution to revenue from these segments as yet.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, profit and the new fee-based businesses, citing record H1 PAT and a 25% first-year AIF return. Cautious on the market backdrop, regulation and risk, which management called a short-term hitch, and it gave no quantified targets for new businesses.

growth.why: Management aims to sustain double-digit profit growth in FY27 and grow to more than 1 lakh customers by 2027, backed mainly by new fee businesses (MTF, merchant banking, insurance, AIF) that are only months old and contribute little revenue yet, with no capacity or order numbers given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Net profit margin was 41.7% in H1 FY27, up 220 bps YoY but down from about 50% in H2 FY26, and new fee businesses are only months old with little revenue yet, so margin direction is unclear.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Flagship branches are planned in high-visibility locations with no count or timeline disclosed, and branch spend is 'on need basis', so timing is uncertain.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets more than 1 lakh customers by 2027 from about 65,000 today, and the MTF book crossed INR100 crores, though the industry F&O volumes were cut sharply in 2026.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capital allocation is tied to MTF and merchant banking growth with branch and technology spend on need basis, and no utilisation or capex figures were given.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance is only double-digit profit growth for FY27 with no quantified revenue or margin targets, and H1 PAT growth of 36.8% already exceeds it, but management has not signalled a raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Weak F&O volumes, higher STT from April 2026, a 6% fall in Nifty in September and MTF rule tightening could slow broking and MTF growth against the double-digit profit guide.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Merchant banking first mandate Apar Advertisers is expected to list within a couple of months, several SME and mainboard mandates are in the pipeline, and QURA Insure advisory started September 2026.

rows.label: Apar Advertisers SME listing
rows.why: First merchant banking mandate is approved and listing is planned within a couple of months, a near-term test of the merchant banking pipeline.

rows.label: QURA Insure insurance advisory scale-up
rows.why: IRDAI corporate agency approval came in July 2026 and advisory began September 2026 targeting 65,000 existing clients, but no revenue has been disclosed and IRDAI commission caps may cut margins.

rows.label: Warrant conversion and fund deployment into MTF
rows.why: 16 lakh warrants at INR234 with 25% received, with proceeds mainly going to MTF and merchant banking, while the MTF book already crossed INR100 crores and industry margin book rose to about INR1.6 lakh crores.

tone.note: Management was confident on record H1 PAT, the 25% first-year AIF return and new fee businesses, but cautious on weak markets, SEBI MTF rules and IRDAI commission caps, and gave no quantified targets; analysts pressed on merchant banking pipeline, dilution, return drivers and MTF collateral risk.
